speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) in the past 10 years, how many foreign students had intentionally defaulted on fulfilling their scholarship bonds; (b) how much scholarship monies has the Ministry managed to recover from these students; (c) how much of such scholarship monies remain uncollected; (d) what is the average length of time taken to recover monies from defaulters; (e) how many defaulters are deemed to be non-contactable anymore; and (f) how much scholarship monies are written off to date.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: For example, since 2014, we have enhanced our data interfaces with partner agencies, such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA), to better ascertain the scholars' employment status.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: I want to reassure the Member that MOE takes a serious view of defaulters.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: It is not just a matter of money, but it is a matter of honour and trust.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: We have managed to recover from a few of these defaulters and the rest will take time as the defaulters are not in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Those who fail to pay their liquidated damages will not be able to work or reside in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: I also want to reassure the Member that MOE does not write off any scholarship monies lightly.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Write-offs are considered only as a last resort and on a case-by-case basis, for example, due to very serious medical conditions and, like I mentioned earlier, it involves only a small number of students.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But there are no numbers given, like how many foreign students there are, apart from the 1% that defaulted and the 4% that are unknown.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, can the Parliamentary Secretary give a comprehensive reply in terms of the numbers?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: How much scholarship monies were written off even though the Parliamentary Secretary had said that MOE does not write off such monies easily?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: How much effort is MOE going to take to recover those monies?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: How far will MOE go to take these errant scholars to task?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I understand it is only 1%, but, as what the Parliamentary Secretary had said, these scholars have tarnished the image and intention of the whole system.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I also agree that there are scholars who are contributing and have become citizens, and these errant scholars have also tarnished the names of these scholars.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, can the Parliamentary Secretary elaborate on this?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Just to put things in context, let me share a bit on the numbers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, only a small proportion of that is spent on international scholars and, of that small portion, 1% of them default, like I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Even though they defaulted because they did not show the intention to fulfil their bond obligations, we will continue to recover from them the liquidated damages.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: A few of them have started to pay back the monies and we will continue to chase the rest of the defaulters for the scholarship monies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the event that they do not pay the liquidated damages, they will not be able to come to Singapore to work or to stay.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to reassure the Member that MOE certainly is reviewing this very seriously and very closely.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I can assure the Member that we will not spare any efforts in ensuring that the steps are taken to monitor and track our scholars to ensure that they understand the gravity of their bond obligations, not just at the point of time when they received the scholarship, but throughout their undergraduate study.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will tighten the process that we have with the university in order to convey the gravity of their bond obligations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: After their graduation, the scholars are expected to update their contact details with us and about their employment status.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will constantly review the system to ensure that we have a robust and also rigorous tracking system to uphold the trust and honour that we expect from these recipients who have the privilege of studying in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I just want to reiterate that even though it is small, this group of people tarnish the whole intention of this foreign scholarship scheme.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The Parliamentary Secretary has said that MOE will take all efforts to recover the cost.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary share what are the efforts that MOE has taken so far?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In my earlier reply, I said that in the last few years, we have strengthened the processes that we have with the relevant partner agencies like MOM and ICA to ensure that we have the data interfaces to know whether the scholars are employed in Singapore and are still in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That is one type of intensification of efforts on that front.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The second thing that we are doing is we are also tightening the coordination with the universities, like I have mentioned, to do a few things.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: One, to convey to the scholars the importance of fulfilling their bond obligations and to stress to them the consequence of not fulfilling the bond obligations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition to that, the MOE team has also placed calls and surveys with scholars to understand their employment status.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These are the few things that we have done and we will continue to intensify efforts to ensure that we have a very robust tracking system, like I have mentioned, to ensure that the scholars fulfil their bond obligations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For those who, for whatever reasons, are recalcitrant and are unwilling to do so, we will ensure that we will have the avenues to recover liquidated damages from them, failing which, like I have mentioned, we will work with ICA to ensure that these defaulters will be banned from working and residing in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary share with us, compared to five years ago, is the current status better or is it worse than before, in terms of the defaulters?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I have updated the House on the various measures that we have taken in the last few years to ensure that we can monitor and track our scholars' abilities to fulfil their bond obligations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We hope to have the Members' understanding that, as you can imagine, this is not just an effort that is within MOE but also coordinating with the universities and also with MOM and ICA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To compile all the data requires a very tight tracking system for it to be very robust.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I have highlighted the various measures that we have taken to address the defaulters and we will continue to build on these efforts.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Actually, I am very glad that out of the 100% of international scholars, only 1%-5% are defaulters.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: For the 95% who abide by the scholarship obligations, how have they contributed to the schooling experience of Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary talk a little bit about that?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And if we look around the world, across the various developed countries, the top universities award scholarships for this purpose.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To benefit their own local cohort; and in our case, to benefit the Singaporean cohort of students with a cross-cultural diversity and exposure.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On the second question, many of these scholars, like I have mentioned, a great majority, have gone on to fulfil their bond obligations and they have gone on to make valuable contributions to their universities, to Singapore and the region.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition to that, they have also helped in a way to promote a better understanding of ASEAN countries and our region amongst our youths.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is important because it builds up Singapore's connections and friendships with these countries around us, strengthening mutual goodwill and relations.
